thread:
maria: hi team, day 2 here. created a hosted API key but getting intermittent 429s when streaming. Is hosted subject to the same sandbox caps?
assistbot: welcome! :wave: Sandbox = low dev quotas. Hosted keys use org quotas which are higher but still enforce per-request and per-token limits. Check Console -> API Keys to confirm key type.
maria: thanks. any quick debugging tips? I see `rate_limit_exceeded` and a Retry-After header sometimes.
sam: check concurrent streams and token rate. streaming counts tokens as they emit; if you open many clients or large max_tokens it can hit rate limits. Also watch for burst of small requests.
maria: ok. is there a standard backoff you recommend?
jen: use exponential backoff with full jitter. example: base 300ms, multiply 2^n, max ~4s. always respect Retry-After when present. For streaming, prefer reducing `max_tokens` or chunking output.
maria: I don't see my usage in Console yet. how do I view my quota?
assistbot: new hires need org mapping. file an IT request at https://redwood.internal/it-requests with subject "map user for quota metrics" and tag @infra.
maria: filed it. last Q: embeddings batch size 32 hit 429 earlier. is that normal?
sam: sandbox has low concurrency. embeddings scale with concurrency, so batching helps but huge batches can still trip request-rate limits. try batch size 8-16 in sandbox.
maria: great, thanks. saved these notes.
jen: one more tip: configure a fallback model in your client config to auto-route to a compatible smaller model if you see capacity errors.
maria: will do, thanks! :thumbsup:
